quarterly_data.signal: Nidec SPMS segment R&D (annual securities report, fiscal year ended March 2026): to address rising data-center power consumption it advanced development of CDUs (coolant distribution units), QDs (quick disconnects) and LCMs (liquid-cooling modules) as high-efficiency cooling solutions for AI servers and other high-performance computing servers (CPU, GPU, memory). The company states it has shipped more than 10,000 In-Rack CDUs cumulatively (as of end-March 2026), establishing a technical edge in the market. It began operating an In-Row CDU in the DRIL (Digital Realty Innovation Lab) inside an MC Digital Realty data center, and completed development of an In-Row CDU for the Google-proposed, OCP (Open Compute Project) compliant 'Deschutes project', which it exhibited at Super Computing 2025 (SC25); it plans to expand its In-Rack and In-Row CDU line-up. It also continues developing higher-efficiency, higher-airflow, higher-pressure and quieter cooling fan motors for air-cooled servers, researched next-generation HDD motors for data storage, where it expects demand to grow with AI servers, and began applied research into physical AI. SPMS R&D spending (including development costs capitalised as intangible assets): JPY 35,487 million.
quarterly_data.figure: In-Rack CDU cumulative shipments more than 10 thousand units (end of March 2026)

quarterly_data.signal: Nidec R&D (annual securities report, fiscal year ended March 2026): R&D expenses in the consolidated income statement JPY 116,903 million (prior year JPY 79,692 million); R&D spending including development costs capitalised as intangible assets JPY 129,887 million. The company is concentrating R&D on five focus business areas: Electrification & Energy Infrastructures (smart grid, BESS, generators and control inverters); Digital Society Solution (AI-server water-cooling systems and cooling fans for data-center thermal management, semiconductor front-end and back-end (packaging) equipment and inspection jigs); Advanced Manufacturing Solutions (humanoid robots, precision reducers, actuators, 3D measurement); Better Life (HVAC, elevators, home appliances); Mobility Innovation (eVTOL and drones). MOEN segment R&D covers battery energy storage systems, power-quality stabilisation systems and generators for industrial and data-center use including backup power; the Group companies business develops AI-server board inspection equipment, semiconductor package electrical inspection equipment and pressure sensors for semiconductor equipment and data-center cooling equipment.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D expenses JPY 116,903 million (prior year JPY 79,692 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Nidec material contracts (annual securities report): its Chinese subsidiary Nidec Appliance Controls (Qingdao) completed the acquisition of 100% of Changzhou Xecom Energy Technologies, a designer and maker of high-performance scroll compressors for air conditioners, heat pumps and freezers (founded 2021), on July 8, 2025 and renamed it Nidec Scroll Technology (Changzhou); the company says the scroll-compressor technology strengthens its freezer presence and lets it enter the air-conditioning and heat-pump markets. Nidec also holds patent cross-licence agreements with NTN (motors using fluid dynamic bearings, mainly for 3.5-inch HDDs; July 24, 2009 to May 7, 2030) and with Panasonic (fluid dynamic bearings and HDD spindle motors; from April 1, 2013 until the licensed patents expire).
quarterly_data.figure: 100% equity interest in Changzhou Xecom Energy Technologies acquired
